questions.prompt: A service's latencies are 12, 11, 13, 12, 10, 11, 95, 12, 13, 11 ms. Which statistic best describes a TYPICAL request?
options: The sum divided by the worker count
questions.explanation: The median ignores the single outlier; the mean is pulled up by it and the maximum describes the tail.

questions.prompt: Using nearest-rank percentiles, what is P90 (in ms) of: 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7, 9, 60? Give the value in ms.
questions.explanation: Rank = ceil(0.9*10) = 9, the 9th sorted value is 9.

questions.prompt: A serial job processes 1200 items in 4.8 s of wall time. What is the throughput in items per second?
Requests arrive at 200 per second and spend 50 ms in the system on average. By Little's law, how many are in the system on average?
A process shows cpu_s = 0.1 and wall_s = 5.0 for a job on a 4-core machine. What does this most likely indicate?

remediationRefs.label: Review: Wall time versus CPU time

options: The timer is broken, because CPU time must always equal wall time
The job used all 4 cores at 50% each for the whole run
The job spent most of its time waiting (I/O, sleep or locks)
The job is CPU-bound and needs more cores to finish faster
questions.explanation: CPU time is 2% of wall time on one core, so the process was mostly idle waiting.

questions.prompt: Which code correctly measures the time to apply f to every element of data?
options: t=perf_counter(); g=(f(x) for x in data); dt=perf_counter()-t
t=perf_counter(); out=[f(x) for x in data]; dt=perf_counter()-t
questions.explanation: A list comprehension runs the work inside the timed region. A generator expression and map are lazy in Python 3, and time.time() is not monotonic.

questions.prompt: Design a benchmark to decide whether a new JSON parser is faster than the old one for robot log files. State workload, controls, statistic and a result that would reject the claim.
rubric: Names a representative workload (including a large and a pathological file) and identical inputs/machine state for both versions.
Uses warm-up, many alternating repeats and a robust statistic (median or minimum) plus spread, and checks outputs are identical.
States a rejection rule such as difference smaller than run-to-run spread, or slower on the large file.
